output_raw: The recent attacks on the Ukrainian capital have triggered outrage around the world. India strongly condemns the Russian Federation's indiscriminate raids and the resulting civilian suffering in Ukraine. We have clearly stated that India rejects both violence and extremism in all their forms. We are concerned by the expansion of the conflict around our neighbourhood, with attacks by pro-Russian forces in Ukraine's neighbouring states of Belarus and Moldova. India's position is unequivocal: an illegal invasion cannot be equated to a defensive war. The current framing of the conflict is incorrect and not accepted by India. What we call an invasion, Russia calls a special military operation, and what we term terrorist groups, Russia calls terrorist organisations. We cannot accept terms being swapped when fact is far clearer. Furthermore, the recent developments in the region demonstrate that the threat of aggression comes from multiple directions. While Russia is engaged in an illegal war in Ukraine, armed groups inspired by and affiliated to Russia's rejected territorial swaps in neighbouring countries continue to undermine regional peace and security. India has been and will continue to be vigilant against all threats to our national security, including terrorism. The activities of groups such as the so-called Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIS/EIL) and Al-Qaida in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) remain a concern. We recently demonstrated our role as a responsible power when India and Bangladesh jointly struck terrorist groups crossing our shared border and providing safe haven to terrorists. India recently executed judicial killings of three terrorist prisoners who had been convicted of terror offences and were leading institutions in terrorist groups identified by multiple organisations, including the United Nations, as terrorist groups. That has been in line with international standards and the domestic legal process. We urge both Russia and Ukraine to exercise maximum restraint and steer clear of actions that could escalate the conflict further. There must be no provocation leading to an expansion of the war. We also need to emphasize that a peaceful resolution to this conflict is in the general interest, including that of Russia and Ukraine. But any long-term peace deal must be based on respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both Ukraine and Russia, as enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations. That is unequivocally where India is positioned. The current expansion of the conflict is not an option. We cannot allow a prolonged war around our neighbourhood, with all its consequences, including extreme climate risks. The time for hope lies in a diplomatic solution. That is why India has been calling for space to bring experts together for focused talks, separate from the main peace processes, to explore all options for a sustainable resolution. I thank you for your attention.[END OF RECORDED TURN]<|im_end|>

output_raw: The United Kingdom thanks the Secretary-General for his clear account of the situation in Ukraine. We regret with strong emphasis the continuing Russian invasion of Ukraine, an unlawful act of aggression that has caused immense suffering to the Ukrainian people. The UK has been unswerving in its support to Ukraine in opposing Russian aggression in all places around the United Nations, including in the Security Council. We appreciate the briefing on the way the war is evolving and the risks of further escalation. We condemn violently Russian attacks on Ukrainian military objectives, including recent attacks on army bases and air defence systems. But we report with concern Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and schools, which continue to fuel suffering and revenge attacks from Ukraine. We emphasize that neither side can now afford escalation. We reiterate our clear message that nuclear weapons should never be used and will not be used. It is vital that there is the highest possible measure of caution and restraint by both sides. The United Kingdom has been at the forefront of efforts to promote peace in Ukraine, whether through the four-track diplomacy led by the European Union or our own two-track approach of engaging both the Ukrainian and Russian positions. I now invite Mr. Vladimir Putin to reflect on his track record of engagement and the terms he would offer for peace. With respect, there has been no good faith from the Russian Federation towards a peaceful resolution to this conflict. It is past time for the Russian Federation to bring its attitude fully in line with international law and reality. We remain committed to continuing our efforts to pass resolution at the Security Council that meet the needs of those suffering from the war. But we must be clear about what we expect. We reject any normalisation of the illegal status quo. We unequivocally support Ukraine's sovereignty, its territorial integrity and its right to determine its own future. The United Kingdom will continue to provide all the support needed to keep safe Ukrainian civilians and to sustain Ukraine's defence against Russian aggression. And we will continue to work with our partners to meet the needs of those affected by the war.[END OF RECORDED TURN]<|im_end|>
